Error messages include the allowed range and the field count (Y/cron.mjs:28, :81), and the RangeError names the expression (Y/cron.mjs:170). Ran npm test: 99/99 pass across test/parse.test.mjs and test/next.test.mjs. The tests cover bounds for every field, many invalid forms, names, the day rule (including */1 and a full range counting as restricted), the 5-year window applied per result, the 2100 non-leap year, n=1000 and the host time zone. About 40 probes and a 300-case fuzz against a brute-force search showed 0 differences. README documents the spacing rules, examples, errors and the per-result 5-year window. Defects (minor): Y/cron.mjs:97-98 and :136 use Array.includes instead of a Set, which is slightly slower. The TypeError for a non-string expr comes from parseExpression after the from and n checks (Y/cron.mjs:157-163); that is fine but the order of checks differs from the task's order. Only spaces count as separators, so a tab is rejected, which matches the task.

A 300-case differential fuzz against Y and a brute-force search showed 0 differences. Defects: X/cron.mjs:108 walks every day for up to 5 years and never skips whole months, so 1000 results of '0 0 1 1 *' took about 66 ms (Y about 13 ms). Tests are thin: X/cron.test.mjs has 18 tests that bundle many assertions, cover few invalid inputs and do not test n=1000 or the host time zone. Y.notes: Ran npm --prefix Y test: 93/93 pass across 9 describe groups, including 5-year window edges just inside and outside, a later gap after the previous result, and no leap day in 2100. X.notes: Ran npm --prefix Y test: 15/15 pass. Probes matched X on almost every case: names, ranges, steps, the either-day rule, leap days, the impossible 30 Feb, and all the error types. Defects: Date.UTC on Y/cron.mjs:89 maps years 0-99 to the 1900s, so next('0 0 * * *', new Date('0050-06-01Z')) throws a false RangeError; splitting on \s+ (Y/cron.mjs:66) accepts tabs, which the spaces-only rule does not allow; Math.max(start, top) (Y/cron.mjs:49) makes day-of-week '7/2' return [0] silently instead of rejecting it. Tests are fewer but have a good list of invalid expressions; most features get only one assertion. The README leaves out the 'only the restricted one counts' half of the day rule and the per-result window.
